investigator.method: NEW investigation against the LIVE public site under policy v1.2, re-starting the probe ladder at Level 1 (not continued/copied from hard-club-porto-01). PASSIVE_STATIC via curl against https://www.hardclubporto.com/ and its agenda page (cold); STRUCTURAL via curl against the publicly-referenced /include/ajax_functions.php AJAX endpoint (funcoes.js), testing both a cold no-session request and, informed by the historical hard-club-porto-01 finding, a warm two-step session-bootstrap request directly at Level 2 -- confirming the full day+month+slug data path without ever needing a browser. Sampled all 22 currently-listed events (11 Sep 2026 - 12 Feb 2027, crossing the 2026/2027 boundary). Tested a candidate deterministic year-derivation rule (event's own canonical URL slug's trailing year, combined with the list's own day+month) against independent first-party corroboration (event titles/descriptions), Hard Club's own retained past-events archive (5 further real year boundaries via 'Happy Neo Year' events), and, per an explicit addendum, Hard Club's own venue-designated linked third-party ticket pages (IRA! worked example plus a 22-event survey). Authored and ran a dependency-free, no-network offline derivation proof (evidence/offline-proof.mjs) reproducing every claim deterministically against retained fixtures.

probe_history.reason:
A plain, cold, unauthenticated GET of the official home page (evidence/home.html) and agenda page (evidence/agenda-cold.html) -- freshly re-acquired for this investigation, not reused from hard-club-porto-01 -- shows the main event list is an empty client-rendered shell:
    , zero server-rendered event cards. No JSON-LD/schema.org block, no RSS/ICS/alternate link. A separate small nav widget (
      ) IS server-rendered even in a cold fetch and shows day+abbreviated-month text (e.g. "11 Set", "12 Set", "13 Set") for only the 3 nearest events -- useful corroboration, but not the full list this investigation needs to sample.

Inspected the page's own public JS (evidence/funcoes.js), freshly re-fetched and re-confirmed to publicly reference the first-party AJAX endpoint /include/ajax_functions.php (action=load-agenda for the list, action=loadevent for per-event price/description/ticket-link) -- not brute-forced, discoverable by reading the site's own script, per this policy's Level 2 definition. A cold, no-prior-session structural GET of load-agenda (evidence/ajax-agenda-cold2.html) reproduces the exact day-only ambiguity ('11 ', no month) both hard-club-porto-01 (v1.1) and the older sources/porto.json note recorded. Per this task's explicit guidance to prefer confirming the known two-step HTTP path at Levels 1/2 without a browser where possible, this investigation then directly tested -- still entirely at Level 2, still zero browser involvement -- whether a normal prior GET of /PT/agenda/ in the same cookie jar (evidence/agenda-pageload.html) changes the AJAX endpoint's response: it does. The warm-session load-agenda fetch (evidence/ajax-agenda-warm.html) returns full day+abbreviated-Portuguese-month text (e.g. "12 Set", "29 Jan", "12 Fev") for all 22 currently-listed events, spanning 11 Sep 2026 through 12 Feb 2027 and crossing the 2026/2027 year boundary. The archive page (evidence/arquivo.html) was also checked for a month/year filter widget; none exists, matching the historical finding. This independently re-confirms, with fresh evidence and without ever needing a browser, the two-step session-bootstrap mechanism hard-club-porto-01 (v1.1) originally discovered via Level 3 browser observation. Because a genuine, reproducible, non-browser HTTP path fully answers the acquisition question, this is logged SUFFICIENT and escalation terminates here -- Level 3 (browser observation) is not attempted in this investigation because it is not needed, not because it was skipped.

start_date.notes: THE central finding of this v1.2 re-investigation. Hard Club's own warm-session AJAX list fragment (evidence/ajax-agenda-warm.html) supplies, for every one of the 22 currently-listed events, TWO separate, retained, first-party pieces of context: (1) a day+abbreviated-Portuguese-month text in the 'data' field (e.g. "12 Set"), and (2) the event's own canonical URL-path slug, which the source ITSELF already uses (per the stable-identifier rule, see source_record_id below) as the DOM id attribute, the /PT/evento/{slug}/ canonical detail-page path, and the id parameter of its own loadevent AJAX call -- and that slug carries a trailing '-YYYY' segment (e.g. "johnny-hooker-euro-tour-2026-2026" -> 2026). Concatenating these two retained, first-party, source-owned signals as YYYY-MM-DD is a fixed, mechanical, exactly-one-result rule -- it does NOT rely on list order/sequence (the historical hard-club-porto-01 (v1.1) investigation correctly refused to do that, and this investigation does not either; see offline-proof.mjs Step 5's finding that Hard Club's own past-events archive list is NOT even reliably chronological). This mapping is not merely assumed: it was mechanically cross-checked, offline, against (a) 6 events' independent first-party title/subtitle/description text (all match, zero contradictions, including both sides of the 2026/2027 boundary: Johnny Hooker '...EURO TOUR 2026', Moonspell Parte II '...HALLOWEEN 2026 PARTE II', Fresno '...EUROTOUR 2027', U.D.O.'s description 'regressam a estrada no inicio de 2027', Lebanon Hanover's description stating the FULL date '21 de Novembro de 2026' directly, Moonspell's description 'Em 2026'); (b) 15 of 22 events' Hard Club-linked, venue-designated, event-specific third-party ticket pages (see the ADDENDUM data_paths entry and evidence/linked-ticketing-survey.json -- these are cited only as ADDITIONAL corroboration, never as the basis itself, since a third-party page cannot supply first-party context under this policy's DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT definition); and (c) 5 further real year boundaries (2017/18 through 2023/24) in Hard Club's own retained past-events archive, via its own recurring 'Happy Neo Year' New Year's Eve events, including one whose OWN title states both years ('HAPPY NEO YEAR! 2018/2019') while its slug/date correctly resolve to 2018-12-31 -- proving the slug tracks the actual occurrence date, not tour-name/season branding. Zero contradictions were found anywhere in the sample. The rule also correctly REFUSES to resolve (rather than guessing) a genuine anomalous archive record whose slug carries no such segment (evidence/offline-proof-output.txt Step 6). Representative value shown here is for JOHNNY HOOKER (12 Set, slug suffix -2026 -> 2026-09-12); all 22 events resolve identically per evidence/offline-proof-output.txt -- 20 to 2026, 2 to 2027 (u-d-o-porto-hard-club-2027 -> 2027-01-29; fresno-eurotour-2027-carta-de-adeus-2027 -> 2027-02-12).

derivation.rule: The event's own canonical URL-path slug (source-owned; used by the site itself as the DOM id attribute, the /PT/evento/{slug}/ canonical detail-page path, and the id parameter of its own loadevent AJAX call) carries a trailing '-YYYY' segment stating the calendar year. The site's own AJAX event-list fragment separately states each event's day-of-month plus abbreviated Portuguese month (e.g. '12 Set'). Concatenate the slug's trailing year with the list's day+month as YYYY-MM-DD; if the slug carries no such trailing segment, the event is left explicitly unresolved rather than assigned any value. This mapping was mechanically cross-checked against independent first-party evidence (each event's own title/subtitle text and/or loadevent free-text description) for every event in the sample where such corroboration exists, with zero contradictions found, including on both sides of the 2026/2027 boundary and across five further real historical year boundaries in the source's own retained past-events archive.

source_record_id.notes: The event's own URL-path slug (e.g. "johnny-hooker-euro-tour-2026-2026") is used consistently, by the source itself, as: (a) the list-fragment anchor's own "id" DOM attribute, (b) the canonical event-detail page URL segment (/PT/evento/{slug}/), freshly re-confirmed via a hidden input on that page echoing the same value, and (c) the "id" parameter the page's own click handler (callEvento in evidence/funcoes.js) passes to the loadevent AJAX action. This matches this policy's stable-identifier rule ("derived from a deterministic source property whose own stability is itself evidenced"). This SAME already-proven stability is what underwrites treating the slug's trailing year segment as reliable DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT for start_date above -- a value the source itself already trusts as its own canonical identity is not merely 'looks like an ID', it is the ID. The fragment's numeric "data-rel" attribute remains confirmed NOT stable (a pagination position index) and must never be used as source_record_id, matching the historical hard-club-porto-01 finding.

event_url.notes: Canonical per-event detail page URL, directly built from the site's own anchor href in the list fragment (evidence/ajax-agenda-warm.html) and freshly re-confirmed by fetching that exact URL (evidence/event-detail-johnny-hooker.html).

price.notes: Exposed via a second, per-event AJAX call (action=loadevent, keyed by the event's own URL slug), not in the main list fragment. Freshly re-confirmed for multiple sampled events at different price shapes: Johnny Hooker "25€- 55€", IRA! "35€" (flat), U.D.O. "45€" (flat), +351 Festival Urbano "22€-30€" (range). The same response also carries an external ticketing link (see the ADDENDUM linked-ticketing analysis) and a free-text description, both venue-authored first-party content.

blockers.description: The full day+month event-list fragment is only returned once the requesting HTTP client has first performed a normal GET of /PT/agenda/ (or another page in the same session) to establish a PHPSESSID cookie, then repeats that same cookie plus a Referer header on the AJAX call. A cookie-naive single-request fetch silently returns day-only text with no error and no different HTTP status -- any future collector must implement this two-step flow explicitly (matches the historical hard-club-porto-01 finding; freshly re-confirmed with new evidence in this investigation).

The list fragment's own 'data-rel' attribute is a small sequential integer that resets across pagination and must never be used as source_record_id -- only the anchor's own 'id' attribute / URL slug should be used (see field_assessment.source_record_id.notes). Matches the historical hard-club-porto-01 finding.

ADDENDUM: Hard Club's own free-text loadevent description for IRA! (evidence/ajax-loadevent-ira-2026.html) states the tour arrives 'em marco de 2026' (March 2026), while the event's own list day/month (03 Out), slug year (2026), and the linked clubedoingresso.com ticket page (which independently states 'Sabado, 03 de Outubro de 2026') all agree on October, not March. This is a genuine internal inconsistency in Hard Club's own marketing copy for this one event -- not a contradiction of the slug/list-derived date (which several INDEPENDENT signals corroborate), but a concrete illustration of why free-text descriptions are not used as the primary basis for any PROVEN field in this investigation.

reasons: Every activation gate in docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md (v1.2) is satisfied against retained, cited, freshly-acquired evidence: identity.status is PROVEN (re-confirmed live, evidence/home.html + evidence/o-hard-club.html + evidence/event-detail-johnny-hooker.html); site_classification.acquisition_class (SPA_API_DISCOVERABLE) is a resolved, supported, non-blocking class; at least one data_paths entry is PUBLIC+CONFIRMED (the warm-session AJAX list fragment); field_assessment.title.state is PROVEN; field_assessment.start_date.state is PROVEN (not UNKNOWN/NOT_PRESENT); field_assessment.source_record_id.state is PROVEN; collector_assessment.recommended_family (STATIC_EVENT_LIST) is a known family; at least one evidence[] item is DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION (evidence/offline-proof.mjs + evidence/offline-proof-output.txt); no unresolved CRITICAL blocker exists (only 3 MINOR); decision.evidence_refs cites supporting evidence.

The v1.2-specific gate is also satisfied: field_assessment.start_date's basis is DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT and it cites ev-offline-proof / ev-offline-proof-output, both evidence_class DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION, proving the slug-year + list-day/month combination was genuinely reproduced offline, not merely asserted.

The calendar YEAR -- the single gap that kept hard-club-porto-01 (v1.1) at HUMAN_REVIEW -- is now honestly resolved for every one of the 22 sampled events via a fixed, mechanical, first-party-only rule (the event's own canonical URL-path slug's trailing year segment, combined with the list's own day+month text), NOT via list order/sequence, NOT via today's date, and NOT via any AI plausibility judgement. The rule was falsification-tested, not merely proposed: 6 independent first-party title/description corroborations (zero contradictions, including both sides of the 2026/2027 boundary), 15 independent linked-ticket-page corroborations (zero contradictions), and 5 further real historical year boundaries in Hard Club's own archive (zero contradictions, including one event whose own title names BOTH years yet whose slug/date resolve correctly) all agree. The rule also correctly refuses to resolve a genuine record lacking the necessary slug context, rather than guessing.

The ADDENDUM's linked-ticketing investigation (IRA! and the broader 22-event survey) provides strong ADDITIONAL corroboration but was deliberately NOT used as the basis for any PROVEN field, because a third-party ticket page -- even one directly, specifically linked by Hard Club's own structured event data -- does not meet this policy's definition of 'first-party context' for DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT. See README.md's LINKED TICKETING ANALYSIS section for the full governance analysis and the smallest concrete change (a new LINKED_TICKETING_SOURCE-style basis/evidence class) that would let it count directly in a future policy version.

This decision is a RESEARCH CONCLUSION ONLY. It does not modify sources/*.json, any venues/*.json registry, manual-coordinates.json, data/public/*, or scheduler configuration, and does not activate a collector. A separate, explicitly-authorised step is required to act on it, per 'Investigation and activation are separate' in docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md.

Each of the 20 pages was fetched once live (2026-08-25) and searched for an exact machine-readable event date (schema.org itemprop="startDate", JSON start_date fields, or 'Comprar bilhetes para DD/MM/YYYY' text), scoped to exclude unrelated 'similar events' carousel blocks appearing elsewhere on the same page. Raw page bytes were not separately retained for all 20 (bounded evidence discipline) -- this file itself, retained under the governed evidence root, is the record of what was mechanically found: 15 of 20 supplied an exact date (all 15 matching the Hard Club slug/list-derived date with zero contradictions); 5 (axisrock/shotgun.live, dr-manuel/weeztix, johnny-hooker/q2ingressos.com.br, rodox/camarotetickets, terrakota/shotgun.live) are client-rendered JS pages with no statically-recoverable date, consistent with the westlive.mticket.eu negative example.
evidence.acquired_from: 20 distinct third-party ticketing URLs (ticketline.pt x6, bol.pt x3, shotgun.live x2, ticketshop.eu x2, and one each of clubedoingresso.com, enterticket.es, weeztix.com, q2ingressos.com.br, camarotetickets.com) -- see field_assessment notes and README.md for the full per-event table
evidence.method: Scripted: `curl -L` fetch of each URL once, followed by fixed-regex (Python) date-pattern extraction; output retained as JSON
